Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (specific reporting line not stated) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s partner role sits at the intersection of a safety-led AI company and an increasingly enterprise-facing ecosystem motion. The work is not simply technical enablement: it requires translating Anthropic’s reliability,
interpretability, and steerability commitments into deployable patterns that external organizations can repeat.

The operating tension is scale versus control. Anthropic needs partners to extend customer reach and implementation capacity, while ensuring that partner-built solutions represent Claude accurately, preserve security expectations, and do
not turn safety positioning into generic AI messaging.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation and AI safety and research company. Its stated mission centers on building reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems that are safe and beneficial.

Its archetype is a hybrid model-platform and ecosystem-led enterprise company. Claude is the product surface, while cloud, technology, and services partners extend how the product reaches and supports organizations.

The company’s central operating challenge is making safety-led differentiation commercially legible in real deployments. Partners must be able to position practical business value without weakening the company’s emphasis on accuracy,
security, reliability, and responsible use.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s flagship product is Claude, positioned as an AI assistant for complex work including data analysis, coding, writing, and problem solving. Its company positioning puts AI safety and research alongside product development rather
than treating safety solely as a compliance function.

The strategic pressure is to turn a frontier AI product into repeatable enterprise adoption. This increases the importance of reusable solution patterns, consistent technical messaging, and disciplined handoffs between product teams and the
ecosystem.

The decision-rights tension is likely between local partner opportunity and centralized product standards. The company needs enough common architecture and enablement to make external delivery scalable, while retaining rapid feedback from
varied customer environments.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic’s public company materials establish a mission spanning research, safety, and product development, but the supplied evidence does not support a detailed named leadership map for this function.

The relevant stakeholder terrain is likely broader than a conventional alliances organization:
- Partner ecosystem owners need commercially usable programs across cloud, technology, and services partners.
- Product and technical teams need structured field signal that distinguishes repeatable product gaps from one-off implementation needs.
- Safety-oriented stakeholders need confidence that scaled partner activity remains aligned with Anthropic’s public commitments.
- External partner leaders need a clear path from Claude familiarity to credible customer delivery capability.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic’s platform message is grounded in reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI. For enterprise architecture conversations, these are not abstract research concepts; they shape how customers and partners evaluate trust, controls, and
deployment readiness.

Claude is marketed as safe, accurate, and secure, with uses spanning knowledge work, data analysis, and software development. This creates a broad solution surface, but it also raises the bar for partner guidance: generic demonstrations are
less valuable than patterns tied to business workflows and operational constraints.

The architecture signal is therefore not a specific vendor stack. It is a need to make Claude’s capabilities usable through consistent solution designs, practical implementation guidance, and feedback loops that improve adoption quality
over time.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly presents a partner network spanning cloud, technology, and services partners. That is meaningful evidence of an ecosystem motion rather than a purely direct, product-led model.

The partnership opportunity is strongest where partners can contribute capabilities Anthropic does not need to build internally: customer access, industry context, systems integration, implementation capacity, and complementary technology.

The likely ecosystem flywheel is:
- Cloud partners broaden access to Claude in enterprise buying and deployment environments.
- Technology partners embed or extend Claude within adjacent workflows and products.
- Services partners convert product capability into organizational adoption and delivery programs.
- Shared deployment experience can surface reusable patterns and product feedback.

A strong partner architecture function should help prevent ecosystem growth from becoming fragmented custom work. Its value is in converting partner activity into repeatable technical and commercial motions.

## Recent Events & Urgency
March 2026 industry reporting described a $100 million expansion of Anthropic’s Claude partner network, including an Accenture training initiative for 30,000 professionals. If sustained, that scale of enablement materially raises the need
for standardized partner readiness and technical quality control.

The urgency is not only channel expansion. Larger partner populations can multiply customer reach, but they can also multiply inconsistent positioning, uneven implementation quality, and disconnected product feedback. Anthropic’s
safety-centered identity makes those risks especially consequential.

The broader frontier-AI market also increases pressure to show that Claude can move from evaluation into durable organizational use. Partners are a route to that scale, but only if they can carry a differentiated and credible deployment
story.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Scale partner-led technical adoption without turning every customer deployment into bespoke advisory work.
- Build repeatable enablement, reference patterns, and technical governance for cloud, technology, and services ecosystems.
- Translate AI platform capabilities into business workflows, implementation decisions, and measurable customer outcomes.
- Balance fast GTM execution with security, reliability, and responsible-AI requirements.
- Lead technical teams that can work credibly with partner executives, architects, developers, and customer sponsors.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s cloud, technology, and services partner network signals a deliberate ecosystem route to enterprise adoption.
- The company’s safety-first identity makes partner technical quality a strategic brand issue, not merely an enablement issue.
- Claude’s applicability across coding, analysis, and knowledge work creates a need for reusable workflow-level solution patterns.
- A scaled partner network needs consistency across technical narratives, delivery practices, and field-to-product feedback.
- The most interesting challenge is likely preserving Anthropic’s differentiated trust posture while increasing partner-led velocity.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, achievements, scope, metrics, leadership experience, and technical expertise must come from the governed resume and proof graph.

Rubric dimensions (graph-only C0.3 augmented skills graph authority, non-SRFS lane):
1. factual_support: claims supported by allowed_fact_packet and candidate claim_ledger source_fact_ids only.
   **For rows carrying `display_override_text`, the authorized substrate is the UNION of `claim_text` +
   `display_override_text`. Phrases from `display_override_text` are deterministically authorized — do NOT
   flag them as unsupported, inferential, or out-of-scope extensions; the generator was X2-required to emit
   them verbatim. When `graph_proof_refs.claim_support_graph_refs` is non-empty, also authorize prose that
   demonstrates those skill nodes; `graph_proof_refs.source_resume_files` is authoritative provenance.
   Cite a `factual_support` failure only when prose deviates from the full authorized union (claim +
   override + graph skill refs).**
2. executive_signal: SVP-level platform/governance/partner-motion synthesis, not bullet stacks.
3. resume_voice: credible executive prose; no recruiter filler, meta narration, or generic AI-company prose, and nothing that would fail a Head of Talent Acquisition screen.
4. ats_alignment_without_keyword_stuffing: JD shapes emphasis only; no JD-as-proof. When allowed facts
   lack EA/interop/federated proof IDs, penalize only if prose invents those themes or ignores documented
   gap_notes — not for absence alone when generation_law_digest requires gap_notes. Reward company-DNA specificity when the
   packet supports partner ecosystem, adoption motion, commercial fit, or a clean Head of Talent Acquisition screen.
5. anti_overfit: no unsupported metrics/credentials; no target company as candidate experience; no repeated metric inventory
   or company-name mirroring; no AI-authenticity dead giveaways such as em dashes, buzzword soup, or template phrasing.
   **`display_override_text` content is NOT an unsupported credential/metric — it is X2-authorized
   substrate. Do not cite override phrases (e.g. "FSA-chartered", "informing data governance and AI
   strategy at scale") as anti_overfit violations.**
6. synthesis_quality: **exactly six** integrated sentences (X2 band); reward connective SVP IT strategy emphasis when
   ledger-backed; penalize thin recap S6, repeated metric surfaces, and bullet-stacked prose. **Do not** soft-penalize
   credential/metric inventory, unused_fact_ids weave targets, or mechanism dumps when the mapped deterministic gate shows `"pass": true`.
   Keep the cadence human enough to pass a Head of Talent Acquisition screen without machine-generated tells.
7. evidence_utilization: when `x2_exec_summary_evidence_utilization` is `"pass": true`, unused_fact_ids are optional weave
   targets — not proof gaps. Penalize under-use only when that gate is `"pass": false` or synthesis is decisively thin;
   reward distinct evidence themes instead of the same metric repeated in multiple sentences.
8. deterministic_alignment: **only** penalize gates that show `"pass": false` in deterministic_gate_summary. Never cite
   retired five-part/S1–S5 arc mandates when gates passed.

Residual quality (always in scope — not closed by X2 alone):
- executive clarity, narrative coherence, commercial fit, usefulness, unsupported phrasing outside ledger scope.

Decisive failure triggers (must align with deterministic_gate_summary failures when cited):
- unsupported business metric or credential (when x2 gates failed or decisive unsupported claim)
- JD or briefing used as proof
- first-person narrative
- obvious rewrite recommendation that invents new claims
